Title: One & Only
Author: Maurene Goo
My Review: This was deliciously juicy and romantic at times, but also Cassia just did some straight-up horrible things. Also she REALLY does not sound like a 40 year old. However, I've been missing chick lit in my life and I mostly enjoyed reading this.

Title: Heart the Lover
Author: Lily King
My Review: Oh my god this HURTSS. This was beautiful- everything from the very pretentious college literary discussions to the <spoiler> heart-wrenching reminiscings at Yash's deathbed </spoiler>. The grief was so painfully well illustrated, I felt it deeply. I need to read some good ol' trash after this, I am upset.

Title: Weyward
Author: Emilia Hart
My Review: This was an incredible read. It was dark and mystical while also being frightfully grounded in reality. The misogyny and abuse were hard to read but very well written. I really enjoyed the narratives of all three generations- although Altha's, being the witchiest and most atmospheric, was my favourite. It is slightly heavy on the tropes, but overall, a good read! Perfect for Halloweekend.

Title: Madonna in a Fur Coat
Author: Sabahattin Ali
My Review: Ah, an actually well written manic pixie dream girl! The writing was beautiful and the ending was tragic (even though I definitely saw it coming). The only reason I can't rate this higher is because of my discomfort with men being obsessed with a woman so early on- without even knowing her.

Title: The Spellshop (Spellshop, #1)
Author: Sarah Beth Durst
My Review: Super cozy and cute- exactly what I wanted from this!

Title: Giovanni’s Room
Author: James Baldwin
My Review:
So deeply emotional. The pleasure, the longing, the sorrow, the internalized shame- it is all so deeply felt. James Baldwin might have just become one of my favorite writers. Every single emotion is captured so beautifully that I felt a sharp stab in my heart, even at the most minute of declarations.
By the end of it, I was in Giovanni's room, being suffocated by every bit of longing and disdain felt by both of them. I cannot bear the thought of Giovanni being left alone.
"You do, sometimes, remind me of the kind of man who is tempted to put himself in prison in order to avoid being hit by a car."
I am crushed by the prose in this book. This is an essential masterpiece.

Title: It Happened One Summer (Bellinger Sisters, #1)
Author: Tessa Bailey
My Review: So problematic, DNFed.

Title: The Unknown (Krewe of Hunters #35)
Author: Heather    Graham
My Review: This is just bad

Title: The Vegetarian
Author: Han Kang
My Review: Definitely thought provoking and the imagery was rich and impactful, but I was left feeling dissatisfied and uncomfortable. That may have been the intention though, I understand why it's sensational.

Title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
Author: Gail Honeyman
My Review:
While Eleanor’s initial antics threw me off, I slowly grew fond of her, much like getting to know a colleague you're unexpectedly paired with and end up understanding. The mix of dry humor and (not so obviously stated) pain was moving. I enjoyed the authenticity of whatever blossoms between her and Sammy, it felt tender and real.

Eleanor’s helplessness was also portrayed so well that when she begins to emerge from it, it feels like a true rebirth. This one left an emotional impact.

Title: We Were Never Here
Author: Andrea Bartz
My Review: The twist was obvious super early, and Emily’s choices were just frustrating. Couldn’t take her seriously, is she blind?

Title: Starling House
Author: Alix E. Harrow
My Review:
I was actually very invested in her backstory and the magic- it's hard to do enough world building in a standalone fantasy book. I think this one does a pretty good job in some aspects, like helping us understand Opal and fleshing out her character, but some threads do seem loose or blurry.
While most of the book had a dark, broody tone (including the chemistry), the chaotic group finale felt a little discordant.

Title: A Court of Wings and Ruin (A Court of Thorns and Roses, #3)
Author: Sarah J. Maas

Title: The Boyfriend
Author: Freida McFadden
My Review: Very easy to read and fast-paced. But there was a sense of expecting the unexpected throughout the book which made the twist become less impactful.

Title: The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches
Author: Sangu Mandanna

Title: I Leave It Up to You
Author: Jinwoo Chong

Title: I Who Have Never Known Men
Author: Jacqueline Harpman
My Review: This was so well done, unlike anything I've read before. <spoiler> I wanted to scream at the end, I really need more answers. But my needs aside, I understand the choices and it's truly masterful. </spoiler>

Title: The Most Wonderful Crime of the Year (Kiss, Merry, Kill, #1)
Author: Ally Carter

Title: The Emperor of Gladness
Author: Ocean Vuong
My Review: Hai's understated emotional turmoil is felt deeply, it touches on how the most unassuming sources can be someone's reason to live. The book dragged on a little bit in the middle. Overall, a very poignant read that is reflective of the human condition.

Title: Broken Country
Author: Clare Leslie Hall
My Review: Such a rich story and such captivating writing! The drama was incredibly engrossing and well written.

Title: Poor Things
Author: Alasdair Gray
My Review: Delightfully strange. I was immediately drawn to the idea of Bella. The change of perspective in the end added so much depth to this story, it was a layer I didn't see coming. Phenomenal storytelling.

Title: Heated Rivalry (Game Changers, #2)
Author: Rachel  Reid
My Review: Of course I read this.

Title: Norwegian Wood
Author: Haruki Murakami
My Review: I was constantly put off by the completely inappropriate thoughts Watanabe had, the lacklustre dialogue, and most importantly, the heinous descriptions of women and their feelings. I'm surprised I finished it, despite physically recoiling from some of the scenes.

Title: The House in the Cerulean Sea (Cerulean Chronicles, #1)
Author: T.J. Klune
My Review: My introduction to TJ Klune was with Under the Whispering Door and I thoroughly enjoyed that story. I went into this with high expectations. It was as heartwarming as expected, but the plot and characters fell short for me. While the messaging was sweet (sometimes excessively so), the antagonists were not fleshed out or complex, the premise was too idealistic, and the magic too inconsequential. The progression of the story was not compelling enough. Maybe I am more cynical now than when I read Under the Whispering Door, but the idea that we can undo such deeply rooted societal prejudices by the accidental kindness of one man is just not a trope I find convincing. Will recommend if you just need a cozy read but not much else.

Title: The Everlasting
Author: Alix E. Harrow
My Review: This was a refreshing romantasy read! It defies every trope I've seen in romantasy books and it was a joy to read about a truly powerful female lead. The time travel stuff got a little tedious at times, but overall, I enjoyed the novelty.

Title: Kaikeyi
Author: Vaishnavi Patel
My Review:
I can't say I know the complete and vast story of Ramayana or the intricacies of all its versions, but I consider myself fairly familiar with the basic story and characters. I wanted to learn more about Kaikeyi's backstory and expected a more nuanced take on what led her to her decisions. However, this book seems to have introduced too many convenient subplots and invented certain traits in other characters just to paint Kaikeyi in a completely innocent light.
While I don't hold strong religious sentiments and always appreciate a flawed hero, the complete character assassination of Ram was off putting. The story deviated too much from the script and I did not enjoy the narrative. There was so much potential but I found it lacking.
Maybe if read without any knowledge of the original epic, it is a decent story.

Title: None of This Is True
Author: Lisa Jewell
My Review:
This was riveting- I couldn't put it down for the first half. The last few plot twists made me uneasy, I cannot overlook the victim blaming.
The ending gave me whiplash- I have no thoughts except that they're all kind of messed up?

Title: My Friends
Author: Fredrik Backman
My Review: Backman does a beautiful job of capturing human connection. The pain, the love, the togetherness- everything was felt so deeply. It made me long for childhood. It made me sorrowful for those who didn't have one. It made me laugh out loud at wit born from trauma. There were a few instances where the profundity felt slightly overdone- but overall, felt a lot of feelings with this one.

Title: All the Colors of the Dark
Author: Chris  Whitaker
My Review: This book reads like an epic- it is a long, poignant, and deeply moving story. The tone throughout is somber and dark but is punctuated with light yet very effective humor (some of Sammy's dialogue had me giggling on the bus!). Somewhere in the middle, the pacing became too slow for me and it took quite some time to get through. Still, I was invested enough to not DNF. The plot and characters were rich and the suspense was highly effective. My heart went out to Saint and Patch, I just wanted them to catch a break. I really liked this book.

Title: Seascraper
Author: Benjamin Wood
My Review: This book is so atmospheric and immersive. I forget that Thomas is 20, he sounds so timeworn and dejected. We feel the sense of hope he feels so acutely when Edgar shows up. This is a great depiction of how one person's hopes and dreams can be built, squashed, and eventually evolve into something more grounded by circumstances. Highly recommend the audiobook- the singing is beautifully done.

Title: The Poet Empress
Author: Shen Tao
My Review: So dark, so brutal! It is such a good story- so very complex and powerful. I think it's one of the best fantasy novels I've read recently. Also who called this a romantasy????

Title: Before I Forget
Author: Tory Henwood Hoen
My Review: This was cute and I enjoyed Cricket's flashbacks of her teenage years. However, it seemed quite unrealistically idealistic- the dementia aspect was handled with great optimism.

Title: Small Boat
Author: Vincent Delecroix
My Review: Very upsetting, the whole thing. Act 2 was chilling. Great book!

Title: The True True Story of Raja the Gullible (and His Mother)
Author: Rabih Alameddine
My Review: This was refreshingly thought-provoking and entertaining at the same time. Raja’s bitter, flippant, grumpy narration is set against grim circumstances, which makes the humor hit even harder. His mother is an absolute riot! A curmudgeonly queer person is one of my favorite perspectives to read from- Raja did not disappoint.

Title: One Golden Summer (Barry's Bay, #2)
Author: Carley Fortune
My Review: This was fun, I loved the great summer imagery. I feel like the mmc and fmc were written like they were in their early 20s, not their 30s, but overall, a good light read!

Title: My Sister, the Serial Killer
Author: Oyinkan Braithwaite
My Review: This had some interesting themes- I loved Korede's complicated thoughts. However, I wish this was more of a thriller than the family drama it turned out to be.

Title: An Academic Affair (Love Notes, #1)
Author: Jodi McAlister
My Review: Not bad! Quite cute, and I love an academic environment.

Title: A Woman Is No Man
Author: Etaf Rum
My Review:
Absolutely heartbreaking. There were many triggering and extremely traumatic parts in this story. I love how it captures the nuances of a deeply oppressive society and how everyone plays a part in keeping it that way. The only gripe I have is that we didn't see a single example of an Arab family that was different from Isra's, this feels reductive.
The ending actually broke my heart- Deya said her last memory of her parents was meeting Adam and then going on a picnic. Knowing what happens to Isra afterwards is just such a brutal way to end a story. Beautifully written.

Title: How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder
Author: Nina McConigley
My Review: I really wanted to like this book, but it did not work for me. It was repetitive and rambling. The story didn't progress very well- we knew almost everything since the beginning. Also what was the point of the quizzes??

Title: The Night We Met (Say You'll Remember Me, #2)
Author: Abby Jimenez
My Review: I don't understand how Mike and Larissa went on for as long as they did. Seemed highly unnecessary. But props to Abby Jimenez for creating the acts of service FINAL BOSS in Chris.

Title: Lula Dean's Little Library of Banned Books
Author: Kirsten Miller
My Review:
This is a good read, but the messaging was a little on the nose. I 100% agree with the message and I enjoyed the various storylines and characters, but I kept thinking about how someone who needs to receive this message will [a] not read this book, and/or [b] not appreciate the blatant preaching.
I did enjoy the occasional humour and the happy (even if highly unrealistic) ending.

Title: Evenings and Weekends
Author: Oisín McKenna
My Review: The fact that I wasn't put off by, like, ten different character perspectives is telling. It's troubling, messy, queer, and thoroughly engaging.

Title: Violet Thistlewaite Is Not a Villain Anymore
Author: Emily Krempholtz
My Review: Cute story- simple and cozy, not much else.

Title: The Apu trilogy (Movie paperbacks)
Author: Robin      Wood
My Review: Profound and thought provoking. Maybe I need to watch the movies now (being Bengali, I should've already watched them 😅).

Title: Rejection
Author: Tony Tulathimutte
My Review:
What did I just read?? In "Feminist," I was initially sympathetic, then slightly less so, and finally disgusted. The second story was so pathetic it made me upset. By the third one, I was just absolutely horrified.
This book is very good, but I did not enjoy it- I am disgusted, rage-baited, and terribly concerned about online presences. Brutal and genius.

Title: Great Big Beautiful Life
Author: Emily  Henry
My Review: You can't tell me those tiny interactions changed their entire lives so much. I also tire of reading things along the lines of "you're like no one I've ever met before." Anyway, I was looking for a light read and this was nice, the romance was good- I see why Emily Henry wins all the Goodreads romance awards.

Title: Martyr!
Author: Kaveh Akbar
My Review:
I have the strong urge to read this again. Very loosely, this book is about mortality, grief, and cultural disconnection. The prose made me stay with the life of someone who I don't necessarily like. There were times when I felt very disconnected from Cyrus, but somehow, that added to the appeal- the need to understand and inhabit his mind.

I, from the bottom of my heart, want the last chapter to imply a happy ending- the surrealism a result of giddiness and a stark shift in Cyrus' perception and his dawning realization of love for Zee; but I am not convinced it is that. "Knowing" Cyrus, I suspect he was dying, not sure from which point in the book, but this was his end, and in true poet fashion, it was beautiful to him.

I enjoyed reading this, although it feels incomplete without some of the plot lines being fully realized. It does not conclude neatly, but that ultimately feels apt.

Title: Thank You for Listening
Author: Julia  Whelan
My Review:
This was repetitive and boring at times. I also did not feel invested in the romance or the main character at all. At the end of the book, I thought, "this could've been an email."

Also I think it's funny that I read two consecutive books with eye-patch donning protagonists lol (All the Colors of the Dark was infinitely better).

Title: Ghachar Ghochar
Author: Vivek Shanbhag
My Review: Despite being short, this book managed to cover some interesting themes. Almost throughout the book, I was infuriated by the narrator and the portrayal of women, although this is probably what the author intended- it is a glimpse of some realities. The writing was compelling but there isn't much of a plot. The last few pages really pull their weight and that's what bumped this up to 3 stars for me.

Title: Leave the World Behind
Author: Rumaan Alam
My Review: This book could've been sooo much more. The premise was interesting and there was an opportunity for a truly captivating plot. Instead, I was constantly pulled out of it by the writing style. The unreliable third-person narration and the comically bad similes made me want to stop reading at least twenty times. Dissatisfying read.

Title: Of Mice and Men
Author: John Steinbeck
My Review: Absolutely devastating.

Title: Sky Daddy
Author: Kate  Folk
My Review: The premise was SO outrageous that I just had to read it. It was so weird and enjoyable in the beginning; but it got tiring really fast. It could've been half the length and had the same impact.

Title: The Grapes of Wrath
Author: John Steinbeck
My Review:
Absolutely Devastating. Depressing AF. 10/10

Note: I listened to the dramatised, abridged audiobook by BBC.

Title: The Wild Robot (The Wild Robot, #1)
Author: Peter  Brown
Publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers

Title: The Mystery of the Exploding Teeth and Other Curiosities from the History of Medicine
Author: Thomas   Morris

Title: Flowers for Algernon
Author: Daniel Keyes
My Review: Absolutely devastating. Getting Charlie's story through his own diary accounts was such a great way to view his changes: growth and subsequent regression. It was upsetting to read about the way he was treated and how his thoughts about that treatment changed over time. Very moving, highly recommend.

Title: Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng
Author: Kylie Lee Baker
My Review: Not for the faint of heart!! This story kept getting gorier and scarier than I'd expected. There is no respite from the evil, it is relentlessly terrifying. I appreciate the narrative and I think it necessarily highlights the systemic and societal injustices of the pandemic era.

Title: The Life Cycle of the Common Octopus: A Read with Jenna Pick: A Novel
Author: Emma   Knight
My Review: I'm not sure what I was supposed to gain from this book. While some parts were interesting, like the intriguing weekend getaway to a literal castle, and the imagery of studying in Scotland, the rest of the book seemed messy and incongruous. I kept trying to discern whether it was about friendship, romance, motherhood, or just suspense? It didn't dwell on any theme long enough for it to count.

Title: Summer Sisters
Author: Judy Blume
My Review: This book kept me captivated throughout- the extent of Caitlin's antics and my constant surprise at Vix tolerating her made me want to see their story through. I can't say I related to the overly romanticized version of "friendship" that was shown in the book though. Also, the occasional POV changes felt unnecessary, I would've been content to read the whole thing narrated by Vix.

Title: The Summer War
Author: Naomi Novik
My Review: This was so cute- the sibling dynamics were complex but wholesome. I enjoy a short fantasy and I think this book does a good job of world building and forming depth without taking too many pages.

Title: The Stranger
Author: Albert Camus
My Review: Meursault is not quite a sociopath but he's not not a sociopath. The writing of his thought process is so detached that much of it felt like reading a catalog, and yet, when the existentialism hits, it hits hard. I don't want to relate to anything he is feeling; but I do at times, and that is scary. Wasn't familiar with your game, Camus.

Title: The Palace of Illusions
Author: Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni
My Review: This was a beautiful read that reignited my love for mythology. I didn’t mind the deviations from the original epic; it was still rich and immersive. While the early chapters dive deep into a short time span and later sections skip over years, I understand the narrative choice. I would’ve happily read more about those skipped years, that’s how invested I was.

Title: The Normal Heart
Author: Larry Kramer
My Review: Brought me to tears, deeply moving.

Title: Rebecca
Author: Daphne du Maurier
My Review: Very well written, the narrator is a deeply fleshed out character. Very immersive and nuanced, would recommend.

Title: Automatic Noodle
Author: Annalee Newitz
My Review: A fun, short read with some interesting thought-provoking themes. There were some inconsistencies but I'm not questioning it too much because it's so short. Overall, I enjoyed the concept and some of the parallels to current affairs.

Title: Ninth House (Ninth House Trilogy, #1)
Author: Leigh Bardugo
My Review: The world building and general setting of dark magic was masterful. The characters were complex and Galaxy's story was moving. I only wish I had more answers without having to read the sequel.

Title: Black River
Author: Nilanjana Roy
My Review: Bleak but gripping

Title: Stag Dance
Author: Torrey Peters
My Review: Powerful read- the discomfort I felt from certain scenes felt like a splash of cold water; needed that.

Title: How to End a Love Story
Author: Yulin Kuang

Title: Bury Your Gays
Author: Chuck Tingle
My Review: After a couple of heavy reads, I picked this up expecting some light trash, but it turned out to be so good! It's unlike anything I've read before, I was hooked.

Title: Everything Is Tuberculosis: The History and Persistence of Our Deadliest Infection
Author: John  Green

Title: The Bell Jar
Author: Sylvia Plath
My Review: I think I waited too long to read this book. While I’m fascinated by Plath’s life, and hence, by the parallels to Esther, I found it hard to enjoy the narrative (maybe that’s the point?).

Title: An Almond for a Parrot
Author: Wray Delaney
My Review: There was something about the blend of period drama, poverty and classism, and magic that drew me in. Interesting read.

Title: There There
Author: Tommy Orange
My Review: Very thought provoking, I felt a deep kind of pain even though I have no personal experience of the emotions depicted in this. Definitely left an impact.

Title: The Paper Menagerie
Author: Ken Liu
My Review: Deeply moving, made me cry on a bus.

Title: Bloody Genius (Virgil Flowers, #12)
Author: John Sandford
My Review: DNFed. Oh my god this felt like staring into a boring CCTV camera feed.

Title: The Club
Author: Ellery Lloyd
My Review: A few too many characters and very entangled storylines, but glamor slightly made up for it.

Title: The Paris Apartment
Author: Lucy Foley
My Review: Honestly super tense read, I enjoyed Jess' perspective. I think the story unraveled nicely.

Title: The Guest List
Author: Lucy Foley
My Review: I liked the eerie island vibes and the moody atmosphere, and pathetic fallacy was on point. The world-building was well done and I stayed interested the whole way through.

Title: Every Single Secret: A Twisty Dark Romance Novel of Revenge and Psychological Suspense
Author: Christina Dodd
My Review: This fell flat for me. The setting was weak, the characters didn’t click, and I couldn’t care less about anyone’s agenda. The villain felt cartoonish, and the motivations were all over the place. I kept waiting to feel invested but it never happened.

Title: The Silent Patient
Author: Alex Michaelides
My Review:
I quite liked this one, it was gripping and hard to put down. The twist was wild, but I did feel a little weird about reading from the murderer’s POV the whole time. It felt like the book was hiding stuff from us just to pull off the surprise.
Still, solid read and definitely kept me hooked.

Title: You Shouldn't Have Come Here
Author: Jeneva Rose
My Review:
This book dragged wayyyyyyy too long. The suspense kept building and building, edging toward something big, but I was so over it halfway through. It felt like the story was trying too hard to be mysterious without actually delivering anything meaningful until the very end.

And that ending? Total gimmick. It felt like a Reddit horror story or one of those copy-pasta shock tales. What could’ve been a chilling short story was stretched into a full-length novel that didn’t justify the page count.

Title: The Woman in Cabin 10 (Lo Blacklock, #1)
Author: Ruth Ware
My Review:
I understand that Lo's anxiety and mental state make her unreliable, but the way her thought process was written annoyed me. She's made out to be this smart journalist, but she seems to be having trouble seeing the MOST OBVIOUS signs of suspicious behavior.
Also, the twist felt poorly timed and the ending felt anticlimactic.

Title: A Flicker in the Dark
Author: Stacy Willingham
My Review: The suspense dragged on for way too long with almost no developments, but the ending was enjoyable.
